content.text: You're a digital creator in Nigeria trying to sell ebooks, courses, or software online. But Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy are unavailable due to platform restrictions, leaving you to navigate a complex and expensive landscape of payment processors. This post provides a detailed breakdown of what options you have, how they compare, and why one architecture is the clear winner for creators in restricted countries.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Gumroad offers a simple way to sell digital products, but it comes with transaction fees and holds your funds for 14 days. Stripe is the backbone of many online businesses, but its availability in certain countries is restricted. Lemon Squeezy is another payment processor with a user-friendly interface, but it too has its own set of fees and limitations. Each of these options requires you to rely on a third-party platform, which means you don't own the infrastructure, and you're at the mercy of their rules and fees.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad's payout delays, Payhip's withdrawal restrictions, and Lemon Squeezy's geographic unavailability all stem from the same root cause: these platforms operate within the traditional financial system. They process payments through Stripe or PayPal on the backend, which means they inherit every restriction those processors impose. When Stripe does not support your country, Gumroad cannot pay you out — regardless of what the platform's feature list implies. Paddle operates as a merchant of record, which creates additional compliance requirements that make it functionally unavailable in most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not platform-level problems. They are financial system problems that only infrastructure built outside that system can solve.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Gumroad charges a 3.5% + $0.30 per transaction fee, while Stripe charges a 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction fee. Lemon Squeezy charges a 2.5% + $0.30 per transaction fee. But what about the real costs of using these platforms? With Gumroad, you're limited to 10,000 transactions per month before you're charged extra. With Stripe, you're required to have a business bank account, and with Lemon Squeezy, you're forced to create a limited company.
